replies: Saved: Knows SQL, Excel and Tableau; 2 years of reporting experience. Is that right?

Your draft fact on file says: "Knows SQL, Excel and Tableau; 2 years of reporting experience." Is that right?

Which of those match a data analyst role — short answer:
- SQL — core skill for data extraction, joins, aggregations, and preparing datasets.
- Excel — essential for quick analysis, pivot tables, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, modeling and ad-hoc checks.
- Tableau — directly matches visualization and dashboarding requirements.
- 2 years of reporting experience — shows domain experience producing regular analyses and stakeholder communication; this maps to "experience with reporting / dashboards" or "business reporting" on postings.
How these translate to common data-analyst job requirements (concrete examples you can cite on applications or in interviews):
1) Data querying and manipulation: "SQL" covers SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, window functions — say "wrote queries to pull and aggregate X" (replace X with a metric when you confirm).
2) Analysis & spreadsheets: "Excel" covers pivot tables, formulas, data cleaning — say "built weekly/monthly performance reports and models in Excel."
3) Visualization & storytelling: "Tableau" covers interactive dashboards — say "created dashboards to track KPIs and presented insights to [stakeholders]."
4) Reporting rhythm & impact: "2 years reporting" becomes "maintained recurring reports, improved report turnaround, reduced time to insight" — quantify if you can (e.g., reduced time by 30%, or supported N stakeholders).

One next step: confirm that draft fact so I can use it in searches and tailor applications (reply "yes" to confirm). If you want, give one quick concrete example to make each skill stronger (a dataset, a KPI you tracked, or a metric you improved).
